clue.text: On the radio get bigger hits

indicators.note: words broadcast on the radio are heard, not seen, so the clue wants a word that sounds like another

parts.note: the moon waxes as it gets bigger

explanation.surface: Broadcast records climb higher in the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the radio' signals a word heard rather than read: WAXES (gets bigger) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: blows struck are whacks, used here as a plural noun for strikes.

clue.text: Let your hair down, as debutantes did?

definitions.meaning: to relax and enjoy yourself thoroughly
debutantes were presented at a formal dance during the season

explanation.definitionFit: Two readings: an idiom for having fun, and literally holding a formal dance.

clue.text: Two tricks opponents at bridge overlook

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
a do is a swindle or trick
North and East sit as opponents at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A pair of bridge opponents miss two tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two tricks' asks for two different synonyms. At bridge the players sit as North, East, South and West, so North and East are on opposing sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to excuse or turn a blind eye to wrongdoing.

clue.text: Country with no popular spring resort

indicators.note: with no means the following piece is removed

parts.note: Spain is a country
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A nation lacking a fashionable holiday spa town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no popular' removes IN from SPAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a town with mineral springs visited for health.

clue.text: In bar posh men only work so hard

indicators.note: the first two pieces are placed in the word for bar, so it opens around them

parts.note: bar meaning except is but
a stag party or stag night is for men only
U is the old label for upper-class or posh usage

explanation.surface: Upper-class men at a gentlemen's bar toil away strenuously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the container; 'bar' looks like a pub but means except, and 'men only' points to a stag party.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to strain oneself with great effort is to work extremely hard.

clue.text: Green stuff found in spaces between walls, say

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken that sounds like another

parts.note: bays are recesses or compartments between walls or columns

explanation.surface: Green material discovered in the gaps between walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks BAYS as heard, giving the green cloth's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the green felt covering of snooker and card tables.

clue.text: One using straw with drink that's an unexpected knockout

parts.note: someone drinking through a straw sucks, so is a sucker
punch is a mixed drink

explanation.surface: A straw-sipper with a cocktail that is a surprise hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One using straw' reads as a drinker but is a person who sucks.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a blow struck without warning, also a nasty surprise.

clue.text: Parisian who enters state positively trembling

indicators.note: the word for who enters the state word, sitting inside it

parts.note: to aver is to state
qui is French for who

explanation.surface: A Frenchman entering a state is shaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian who' asks for the French word, which 'enters' the verb for state.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: quivering, trembling all over.

clue.text: Couple of followers turning up, not outsiders

indicators.note: not outsiders means the end letters are removed
in a down clue, turning up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a retinue is a body of followers

explanation.surface: A pair of supporters arrive, excluding those not in the circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses RETINUE to EUNITER, and 'not outsiders' trims its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to couple is to join or link together.

clue.text: Saint leaving disguised as evil manipulator

indicators.note: letters disguised are rearranged so the word is not recognisable

explanation.surface: A holy man departs wearing a disguise as a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' signals the anagram of the clue's own word 'leaving', which looks like the verb for departing.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: the hypnotist in du Maurier's Trilby gave his name to any sinister controlling figure.

clue.text: Address used among sovereigns one crossing America

indicators.note: one piece runs across the other, so it holds it inside

parts.note: one sovereign, read as a gold piece of money, is a coin
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: Monarchs use a form of address when one travels across America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' picks up the sovereigns of the definition as coins: a COIN crossing (holding) US. Monarchs traditionally call each other and their senior nobles by this kinship term.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal usage: kings and queens formally address fellow monarchs and peers as a relative, this term.

clue.text: Passage seen by judge during ramble around castle, say

indicators.note: the passage word is placed beside the first part
the judge appears during the ramble, so its letter sits inside
around signals that the ramble word is turned back to front

parts.note: to ramble is to roam
a passage of writing or music is a piece

explanation.surface: A judge's text is examined while walking round a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns ROAM to MAOR, and 'during' puts J inside it. 'castle, say' is chess: the rook is a major piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in chess the castle, or rook, is one of the heavy pieces along with the queen.

clue.text: Fact I point out at start of every pope's reign

indicators.note: out signals the letters are disordered
only the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: The basic fact begins every papal reign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges FACT I POINT; 'at start of every' adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: the office or term of a pontiff, his papacy.

clue.text: Struggle with sight

parts.note: to struggle against someone is to vie

explanation.surface: Battling against poor eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sight, as in a fine prospect, is a view or vista.

clue.text: Spice Girl entertaining Conservative leader

indicators.note: the girl entertains a guest, so the other letter goes inside her name

parts.note: Mae is a girl's name

indicators.note: a party's leader is taken as the word's first letter

explanation.surface: A Spice Girl hosts the head of the Tory party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spice Girl' reads as the pop group, but 'Spice' is the definition; 'leader' takes C, and 'entertaining' puts it inside MAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the lacy outer covering of nutmeg is ground as a culinary spice of this name.

clue.text: Pry or sneak around being a busybody

indicators.note: the letters move around into a new order

explanation.surface: Snooping and creeping about like a meddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges the letters of PRY OR SNEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an inquisitive meddler into others' affairs is a British idiom for a snoop.

clue.text: Customary scenery a TV series declined

definitions.meaning: fixed or usual, as in a habitual routine
the stage scenery for a play
a collection or group of things
having gone down, as the sun does

explanation.definitionFit: Five senses of the same short word: usual, stage décor, television, group, and sunk.

clue.text: Charging a lot without thinking

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
pensive means deep in thought

explanation.surface: Billing heavily, done thoughtlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without thinking' reads as careless, but splits into two pieces: the Latin-derived prefix for without and an adjective for lost in thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: costly, demanding a high price.

clue.text: Disreputable female's list, including endless beer

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female

indicators.note: the list word includes the beer inside it

parts.note: a ship that lists leans to one side

indicators.note: endless removes the final letter

parts.note: bitter is a British style of beer

explanation.surface: An unsavoury woman's register includes some unfinished ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of the beer, and 'including' places what is left inside the list word, after its A. Bitter is a hoppy British draught beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: something shabby or squalid, as if infested, is called seedy or down-at-heel.

clue.text: Touching land in a way

indicators.note: the land word goes in the other pieces

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
to land a prize is to gain it

explanation.surface: Moving to earth in a particular manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container: the land word sits between A and the abbreviation for street.
explanation.definitionFit: Preposition: in contact with, as a ladder leaning on a wall.

clue.text: Main provider of awfully good exercise?

parts.note: pi is slang for sanctimonious or pious, too good
PE is physical education, exercise at school

explanation.surface: The chief source of really beneficial exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully good' means smugly virtuous, PI, not a strong compliment.
explanation.definitionFit: Function: a water main is a large conduit that delivers supply, so a tube is what provides it.

clue.text: Play on words about girl being a prude

indicators.note: the pun goes about, surrounding the girl

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A joke about a woman being a straitlaced type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals that the play on words goes round the girl's name; 'being a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a person with very strict morals, a killjoy.

clue.text: Suit a source of joy? Not sure

indicators.note: not removes the following word from the longer one

parts.note: a pleasure is a source of joy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is a lawsuit a joy to pursue? Uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not sure' looks like doubt but means remove SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal sense: a suit brought in court involves an appeal or entreaty, a pleading.

clue.text: How Jersey communicated tax, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals a word spoken that sounds like another

parts.note: a tax is a burden or load

explanation.surface: How the island spread news of a levy, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' suggests the Channel Island but is the breed of cow, which mooed.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a cow makes its sound by mooing.

clue.text: Confused doctors not nice with her

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Muddled physicians are rude to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctors' looks like physicians but is a verb, rearranging NOT NICE and HER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a muddled or rambling manner of speaking is unclear and disjointed.

clue.text: He wrote chapter to entertain mainly

indicators.note: mainly takes most of the word, dropping its last letter

parts.note: to amuse is to entertain

explanation.surface: An author's chapter is mostly for entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' cuts AMUSE to AMUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Albert, the French novelist of The Outsider.

clue.text: Duck out of quarrel with a country

indicators.note: the duck is taken out of the quarrel word

parts.note: a row is a quarrel
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
and means with

explanation.surface: Leaving a fight with someone from another nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is cricket's zero, O; 'out of' takes it from ROW to give RW.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an East African republic, landlocked and hilly.

clue.text: Carry on or declare

definitions.meaning: to state firmly as true, to assert

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to keep something going, and to insist something is so.

clue.text: Monkey about in playgroup, mischievously

indicators.note: about turns the found letters round
in shows the letters are found inside the words

explanation.surface: Monkeying around at nursery in a naughty way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds PMI across grouP MIschievously, and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a rascally child, a little monkey.

clue.text: Leading journalist resisted changes

indicators.note: changes says the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A top newspaperwoman fought off reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges RESISTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated term: a woman in charge of a publication, its chief journalist.

clue.text: Artist ignoring a dramatist

indicators.note: ignoring the letter means it is left out

parts.note: a painter is an artist

explanation.surface: A painter overlooking a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring a' drops the A from PAINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Harold, the British playwright of The Caretaker and Nobel laureate.
